name: Veigar
notes: Veigar spends the fight casting rather than attacking, so "attack": {"never": true} is set and items that key on attacks or attack speed give him no value here.
Casts go one at a time: Q, W and R each have a 0.25 s cast time (the dossier's castTime), during which no other cast can start. Each keeps a single busy_until that a cast pushes to t + 0.25 s.

Opening: the engine's automatic t=0 cast fires Primordial Burst (R), which occupies Veigar until 0.25 s; Baleful Strike (Q) then starts at 0.25 s (done at 0.5 s), and Dark Matter (W) starts at 0.5 s (done at 0.75 s). From then on Q and W are each cast again as soon as their own cooldown AND the shared busy_until allow it, for the rest of the fight.

Dark Matter's damage lands 1.2 s after its cast begins (the delay starts at the beginning of the cast time, per the wiki) and is snapshotted from Veigar's AP at the moment of casting, not at impact; the impact landing itself is not a cast and does not block other casts.

Each Q, W or R cast that lands on the dummy grants +1 stack of Phenomenal Evil Power (and thus +1 AP), applied with the hit itself so it can only boost later casts, matching the wiki's 'added immediately on enemy kill (on next game tick)' wording for the analogous takedown-stack case; this is an unsettled reading (low impact per the dossier).

Dark Matter's cooldown is base 8 s multiplied by 0.9 for every 50 stacks of Phenomenal Evil Power accumulated, then further reduced by the build's ability haste; within an 8-15 s fight stacks rarely cross the first 50-stack threshold, so it stays close to its flat 8 s base.

Event Horizon is never cast (see "unused"): it deals no damage, and whether a stationary dummy standing at the cage's center ever registers as 'touched' by the cage edges (and so grants a Phenomenal Evil stack) is left open by the sources; either way its value would be marginal next to spending that same cast time on Q or W.

Primordial Burst is cast at t=0 (the engine's automatic opening cast) and again whenever it comes off cooldown (60-120 s by rank) rather than held for the missing-health execute cap: the sources leave that timing call open, and since it is a single-cooldown ability, holding it risks it never landing in a short or high-HP fight and losing all of its damage rather than the smaller loss from an early, lower-multiplier cast.

Primordial Burst's damage multiplier is 1 + 1.5 x the target's missing-health fraction, capped at 2x (equivalent to the wiki's 66.66% missing-health cap); its listed projectile has no travel-time number in the sources, so its damage is treated as landing with its 0.25 s cast, the same as Q.
Mana costs are not modeled: nothing here binds inside a short fight at level 16 with a typical item-built mana pool.
The +5 stack bonus for an enemy champion takedown never applies, since the dummy is never actually killed by the engine.

unused.E: Event Horizon deals no damage (a pure stun/knockdown), so it is never cast; casting it would only cost cast time and mana that Q or W spend on damage instead.
